mcq.q: What is an election?
options: A process where people vote to choose leaders

mcq.q: What is a candidate?
options: A person who stands to be elected

mcq.q: What is a ballot paper?
options: A paper on which a voter marks a choice

mcq.q: Why should voting be secret?
options: So that nobody can force how you vote
So that the winner is hidden

mcq.q: What does majority mean?
In an election, 12 pupils voted for Amina and 10 for Brian. Who wins?
A candidate gives sweets for votes. What is this?
What is campaigning?
options: Telling voters why they should choose you

mcq.q: What should you do if your candidate loses?
options: Refuse to work with the winner
mcq.explanation: Accepting results is part of democracy.

mcq.q: Which shows respect for the minority?
options: Listening to those who did not win

mcq.q: What is a suggestion box used for?
What is a mock election?
mcq.explanation: A mock election teaches how voting works.

mcq.q: Which of these is a benefit of democracy in school?
At what age can a Kenyan vote in national elections?
mcq.explanation: Adults aged 18 and above can vote.

mcq.q: How often are general elections held in Kenya?
mcq.explanation: Kenya holds general elections every five years.

mcq.q: What are tally marks used for?
How many tally marks does a group of five look like?
options: Four lines crossed by one line
mcq.explanation: A group of five has four vertical lines and one crossing them.

mcq.q: What does equality mean in an election?
options: Each person has one vote of equal value

mcq.q: What is a Children's Government in school?
options: A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
mcq.explanation: It is made up of pupils chosen by their classmates.

mcq.q: Who usually guides a Children's Government?
mcq.explanation: A teacher adviser guides the pupils.

mcq.q: How are members of the Children's Government chosen?
Who leads the meetings of the assembly of pupils?
What does a class representative do?
options: Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
mcq.explanation: Class representatives speak for their classmates.

mcq.q: Who takes over when the president of the Children's Government is absent?
mcq.explanation: The deputy helps and takes over.

mcq.q: Who writes down what is discussed and decided at a meeting?
Which is a function of the Children's Government?
options: Helping to keep order and cleanliness
mcq.explanation: Leaders help with order and cleanliness.

mcq.q: Which minister would deal with dirty toilets?
mcq.explanation: Health and sanitation looks after cleanliness.

mcq.q: Which minister would organise a football match between classes?
What should a Children's Government NOT do?
What does a patron do?
options: Guides and advises the pupil leaders
mcq.explanation: The patron is a teacher adviser.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way of participating in the Children's Government?
What is an agenda?
options: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
mcq.explanation: An agenda gives the order of business.

mcq.q: Which item usually comes first on an agenda?
Which item usually comes last on an agenda?
Which quality is important for a pupil leader?
mcq.explanation: Leaders must be honest and fair.

mcq.q: Which shows respect for the Children's Government?
Which is the right way to make a complaint?
Why is a Children's Government important?
options: It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility

mcq.q: In a mock session, what should pupils do first after opening?
mcq.explanation: Minutes remind the group of past decisions.

mcq.q: What is the meaning of composition of a group?
options: The people or parts that make up the group
mcq.explanation: Composition means the members that make up a group.

mcq.q: What is a community?
options: A group of people who live in the same area and share things
mcq.explanation: People in a community share a market, a school or customs.

mcq.q: Who is a leader?
options: A person who guides and helps others to do something good

mcq.q: Which of these is a religious leader?
Which of these leads prayers in a mosque?
What is a clan?
options: A large family group with a common ancestor
mcq.explanation: A clan traces its origin to one ancestor.

mcq.q: Who leads a clan?
What do clan elders do?
mcq.explanation: Clan elders guard customs and settle quarrels.

mcq.q: What do village elders do?
options: Welcome visitors and help settle small quarrels

mcq.q: Who leads a location and is appointed by the national government?
Who leads a sub-location?
mcq.explanation: An assistant chief leads a sub-location.

mcq.q: Which duty belongs to a religious leader?
Which quality means treating everyone equally?
Which quality means telling the truth?
Which quality means not boasting or looking down on others?
Which action shows good leadership?
options: Sharing food aid equally and recording it
mcq.explanation: Fairness and honesty are good leadership.

mcq.q: What happens when leaders are dishonest?
options: Trust is lost and resources are wasted

mcq.q: Who is a good resource person to learn about community leadership?
Which activity can show leadership qualities in class?
options: Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
mcq.explanation: Role play shows how leaders act.

mcq.q: How can you show respect for community leaders?
options: Listen politely and follow fair rules
mcq.explanation: Respect means polite listening and obeying good rules.

mcq.q: Why is it important for leaders to have good qualities?
options: People trust them and live in peace
mcq.explanation: Good leaders build trust and peace.

mcq.q: How many county governments are there in Kenya?
mcq.explanation: There are 47 counties, each with its own government.

mcq.q: What is devolution?
options: Keeping all power in one place
Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments
mcq.explanation: Devolution moves some power to counties.

mcq.q: Which law created county governments in Kenya?
Who is the head of a county government?
Who helps the governor?
mcq.explanation: The deputy governor supports the governor.

mcq.q: Who elects the governor?
mcq.explanation: Voters in the county elect the governor.

mcq.q: How often are governors elected?
mcq.explanation: General elections are held every five years.

mcq.q: What does MCA stand for?
mcq.explanation: MCA is a Member of the County Assembly.

mcq.q: How many MCAs does each ward elect?
Who leads the meetings of the county assembly?
What does the county assembly do?
options: Makes county laws and approves the budget
mcq.explanation: The assembly makes laws and approves the budget.

mcq.q: What does the county executive do?
options: Carries out the laws and runs county services

mcq.q: Which of these is a county government service?
mcq.explanation: Health centres are a county responsibility.

mcq.q: Which of these tasks belongs to the county government?
mcq.explanation: County roads belong to the county.

mcq.q: Which of these is a national government service?
What are ECDE and pre-primary schools run by?
mcq.explanation: Pre-primary education is a county function.

mcq.q: Where does a county government get money?
options: From the national government and local fees and taxes
mcq.explanation: Counties get shared money and collect local fees.

mcq.q: Who is closest to the people among county administrators?
mcq.explanation: Village administrators work closest to families.

mcq.q: What is public participation?
options: Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget

mcq.q: Which best describes the difference between the governor and an MCA?
options: An MCA is above the governor
The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor

mcq.q: What is a duty of an MCA?
options: Represent the people of the ward in the assembly

mcq.q: Who approves the governor's choice of county executive committee members?
Why do we have county governments?
options: To bring services closer to the people
mcq.explanation: Counties bring services near to people.

mcq.q: Who is the head of the national government?
mcq.explanation: The President leads the national government.

short.q: Explain how a village elder can help two neighbours who quarrel about a fence.
short.answer: Listen to both, be fair, help them to talk and agree, and encourage them to forgive.

short.q: Explain what may happen in a community with dishonest leaders.
short.answer: Resources are wasted, people lose trust, and people quarrel.

short.q: Describe how a class can invite a resource person to talk about leadership.
short.answer: Write a polite invitation, state the topic, give the date and time, and thank the visitor after the talk.

short.q: Explain the difference between a chief and a clan elder.
short.answer: A chief is appointed by the national government to lead a location. A clan elder is respected by a clan for age and wisdom and keeps customs.
short.working: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

short.q: Design a poster: write a slogan and list three qualities of a good leader you would show on it.
short.answer: A slogan such as A Good Leader Serves, and qualities such as honest, fair and kind, with a picture.
short.working: 1 mark for a slogan, 3 marks for three qualities, 1 mark for a picture.

short.q: Explain what devolution means.
short.answer: It means sharing power and resources between the national government and county governments.
short.working: 1 mark for sharing power, 1 mark for national and county.

short.q: State three reasons why Kenya has county governments.
short.answer: To bring services closer to people, to let people take part in decisions, and to share development fairly.

short.q: Name the two main parts of a county government and state what each does.
short.answer: The county executive runs the county and carries out laws. The county assembly makes county laws and checks the executive.
short.working: 1 mark for each part and 1 mark for each job.

short.q: State three duties of the governor.
short.answer: Lead the county executive, present the budget and plans, and represent the county.

short.q: State three roles of an MCA.
short.answer: Represent the ward, make county laws, and approve the budget. Accept checking the governor.

short.q: Give four services provided by county governments.
short.answer: Health centres, county roads, pre-primary schools and markets. Accept cattle dips or water services.

short.q: Explain the difference between the governor and the president.
short.answer: The president leads the national government of the whole country. The governor leads one county government.
short.working: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

short.q: Describe the duties of ward and village administrators.
short.answer: They bring county services close to people, pass on information, help organise public meetings, and take the community's needs to county leaders.

short.q: Explain how citizens can support the county government.
short.answer: Attend public meetings, vote, pay fees and taxes, and take care of public property.

short.q: Explain why the county assembly must check the work of the governor.
short.answer: To make sure county money is used honestly, to prevent misuse of power, to make sure services reach people, to protect citizens' interests, and to keep the governor accountable.

short.q: What is a compass used for?
short.answer: A compass is used to find direction. Its needle points to north.
short.working: 1 mark for finding direction, 1 mark for the needle pointing north.

short.q: State two things a good map key should show.
short.answer: The meaning of the colours and the meaning of the lines or symbols used on the map.

short.q: What is the difference between a lake and a river?
short.answer: A lake is a large area of water with land around it. A river is water flowing along a channel to a lake or ocean.

short.q: Name two water features found in Kenya.
short.answer: Lake Victoria and the Tana River. Accept Lake Turkana, Lake Naivasha or the Indian Ocean.

short.q: Give two reasons why farmers plant crops at the start of the rainy season.
short.answer: The rain gives the seeds water to grow, and the wet soil is soft to dig.

short.q: Why should you never shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm?
short.answer: Lightning can strike tall trees. It is safer to go into a strong building.
short.working: 1 mark for the danger, 1 mark for a safer choice.

short.q: Name two historic places in Kenya and the town or county where each is found.
short.answer: Fort Jesus in Mombasa and Thimlich Ohinga in Migori County. Accept Lamu Old Town or Gede Ruins.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct place with its location.

short.q: Why do people trade?
short.answer: People trade to get the goods they need but cannot make, and to earn money from the goods they produce.

short.q: What is meant by a densely populated area?
short.answer: An area where many people live close together.
short.working: 1 mark for many people, 1 mark for close together.

short.q: Name two artefacts made by communities in Kenya.
short.answer: A kiondo basket and a soapstone carving. Accept clay pots, beaded jewellery or wooden stools.

short.q: What is a school motto?
short.answer: A motto is a short sentence that shows what a school stands for or hopes to achieve.
short.working: 1 mark for short sentence, 1 mark for showing what the school stands for.

short.q: Give two reasons why we obey school rules.
short.answer: Rules keep everyone safe and they help everyone to learn.

short.q: Give two examples of natural resources.
short.answer: Water and soil. Accept forests, minerals, wildlife or fish.

short.q: Explain what a raw material is and give one example.
short.answer: A raw material is a material used to make something new, for example sugarcane used to make sugar.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

short.q: How do you calculate profit?
short.answer: Profit is found by subtracting the costs from the income.
short.working: 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for costs from income.

short.q: Name two duties of a pupil in school.
short.answer: Follow the school rules and respect others. Accept care for property or do class duties.

short.q: What does the Kiswahili word amani mean and why is it important in a school?
short.answer: Amani means peace. It is important because pupils feel safe and can learn well.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 mark for the reason.

short.q: Where can a child go for help if they are being harmed?
short.answer: To a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher, or to the child helpline 116.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct source of help.

short.q: What is a majority?
short.answer: The larger number of votes, more than any other choice.
short.working: 1 mark for larger number, 1 mark for votes.

short.q: Who is the patron of a Children's Government?
short.answer: The patron is a teacher who guides and advises the pupil leaders.
short.working: 1 mark for a teacher, 1 mark for guides the pupil leaders.

short.q: Who is a clan elder?
short.answer: A clan elder is an older respected member of a clan who leads it and keeps its customs.
short.working: 1 mark for respected older member, 1 mark for leading or keeping customs.

short.q: What is a county assembly?
short.answer: The county assembly is the group of elected members (MCAs) that makes laws for the county.
short.working: 1 mark for group of MCAs, 1 mark for making county laws.

short.q: Write a short motto for a school and say what it means.
short.answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It means pupils should study well and be kind to others.
short.working: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for its meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

short.q: Describe how you would prepare a poster on the school values.
short.answer: Choose the values, write a large title, draw a picture for each value, and use bright colours that can be seen from far.
